headline: Nasdaq slumps 2.1% and Brent touches $110 intraday; BTC ETFs took in just $5.1M on 10/15 (prelim.), still −$742M over 7 days, yet weighted funding climbed back to 9.81% — leverage is returning before spot money.
summary: A tech sell-off and the Hormuz oil shock put risk assets under pressure again; BTC held above $80K but closed at 38% of its daily range, below the value area. ETF buying has not returned and the Coinbase premium stays negative while leverage is rebuilding, so the flow picture is weak. Market stage remains Bull (day 8); no exit rule fired or is close. Next: whether ETFs post consecutive inflows, the Oct 27–28 FOMC and MSCI's Nov 11 list.

news.title: AI-led tech sell-off continues: Nasdaq closes −2.14% at 26,140.03, −4.5% on the week (worst since late June); S&P 500 −1.09%; VIX up ~21% to 19.99
news.read: BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.668 on this site, so tech is the main weight on BTC these days; BTC fell only 0.77% and held above $80K, outperforming the Nasdaq. A short-term cross-asset backdrop; it does not touch the 200-day MA (−11.2%) or any exit rule.

news.title: Iran steps up tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent touches $110 intraday (first since May), WTI settles at $99.04 (+2.63%); Kpler: Hormuz crude flows 11.62M b/d in the week to 10/13, ~32% below baseline
news.read: Higher oil means sticky inflation; stacked on hot CPI and PPI prints it keeps hike expectations alive, with the 10-year at 5.10% and real yield at 2.78% still elevated. A macro headwind for BTC, but only price and funding backdrop — it does not change the market stage or exit framework.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs net +$5.06M on 10/15 (SoSoValue $5.055M, Trader T $5.07M): IBIT +$16.8M, Grayscale BTC −$7.64M, BTCO −$4.09M, 8 funds incl. FBTC and GBTC flat
news.read: The two sources are within 2%, so the site lists it as a preliminary 10/15 value. Outflows paused but there is almost no new buying; the seven complete days 10/06–10/14 total −$742.4M, and with a Coinbase premium of −0.142% US spot demand is still weak. Realized cap +1.28% over 30 days stays positive; the market stage is unchanged.

news.title: Fed Chair Warsh offers no new rate signal at the IMF/World Bank meetings in Bangkok; 10-year ~5.09%; CME December hike odds 74.3% (50.2% a month ago), October expected on hold
news.read: The Oct 27–28 FOMC is expected to hold, but markets now price a December hike; high rates keep capping valuation expansion. The site's real yield is +10 bp over 20 days, milder than last edition (+22 bp). Macro backdrop, not a framework condition.

news.title: MSCI finalizes its non-operating company rules: failing 4 of 5 financial ratios makes a firm ineligible, existing members must fail two consecutive annual periods before removal; list on 11/11, effective after the 11/30 close; Strategy and Metaplanet were in the initial assessment
news.read: Exclusion would not force Strategy to sell BTC, and JPMorgan's earlier $2.8B passive-selling estimate applied to the old proposal; the two-period clause lowers the odds of immediate removal. It affects treasury companies' funding access; the site has no direct indicator for it — a medium-term institutional backdrop.

news.title: 24h market-wide liquidations fall to $290M (from $929M the day before); BTC liquidations ~$56M (from $214M)
news.read: Liquidations are back to normal, but the site's weighted funding rose to 9.81%, so leverage is rebuilding quickly after the flush; funding is not extreme and the −2.97 risk reversal still leans protective. Short-term noise; it does not affect the cycle call.

news.title: French bitcoin treasury firm Capital B posts an H1 net loss of €69.5M (~$78.1M), including a ~€67.5M BTC impairment
news.read: An accounting impairment from prices below cost at end-June; together with MSCI's rules it shows pressure on the treasury-company model. These firms were one source of demand, so slower buying extends weak non-ETF demand. No direct effect on the site's on-chain or cycle indicators.
